featured.title: Sundar Pichai Is Paying Elon Musk $920 Million a Month to Rent GPUs. That's the AI Economy Now.
featured.excerpt: Google's Alphabet signs a $920M monthly deal with SpaceX for 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs, just days before SpaceX's record-breaking $1.77 trillion IPO.

featured.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai, born in Chennai and educated at IIT Kharagpur, is at the helm of the company signing one of the largest compute rental deals in history. For NRI investors, the SpaceX IPO is pulling global capital away from Indian markets — forcing a portfolio decision between the AI infrastructure buildout and emerging-market exposure.

nri-world.title: The Rupee Crossed 95. For NRIs Wiring Money Home, Every Dollar Now Buys a Small Fortune.
nri-world.excerpt: India's currency has shed 12 per cent against the dollar in a year — a gut punch for importers, but an unexpected windfall for the diaspora sending money back.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes; the currency has lost over 12 per cent against the US dollar in the past year
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances to India are getting significantly more rupees per dollar, affecting family support, property purchases, and retirement planning for millions abroad.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Gulf NRIs Are Buying Indian Stocks While Wall Street Runs for the Door. The Numbers Explain Why.
nri-world.excerpt: Foreign institutional investors have yanked $31 billion from Indian equities this year. GCC-based NRIs, meanwhile, are doing the opposite — and SEBI just made it easier.
nri-world.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; foreign investors have withdrawn a record ₹2.67 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Gulf NRIs are taking a contrarian long-term bet on Indian equities even as global institutional money flees, reshaping how diaspora wealth flows into India's capital markets.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Cuisine Got Its Own Davos in London. Sanjeev Kapoor Walked Away With the Top Prize.
nri-world.excerpt: The inaugural global Indian Restaurant Congress & Awards brought 250 chefs, restaurateurs, and hospitality executives to the Royal Lancaster London — and launched a new industry platform for the UK's 12,000 Indian restaurants.
nri-world.image_caption: Sanjeev Kapoor, named Global Indian Chef of the Year at the inaugural London congress
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's Indian restaurant sector employs 100,000 people and represents the diaspora's transition from immigrant enterprise to global culinary export. The congress, backed by Lords and MPs, formalises what NRI chefs have built over decades.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Seven Indian Workers Died on a Dubai Highway on Monday. Their Families Are Now Navigating the Hardest Part.
nri-world.excerpt: A minibus carrying labourers rear-ended a broken-down truck on Emirates Road, killing seven and injuring nine. The Indian Consulate confirmed it is coordinating hospital visits and repatriation.
nri-world.image_caption: Dubai's highway skyline — Emirates Road, where the collision occurred, is one of the emirate's busiest arterial routes
nri-world.nri_angle: India receives roughly $15 billion in remittances from the UAE annually, generated overwhelmingly by blue-collar workers in dangerous transport and construction jobs. When they die abroad, families face a labyrinth of embassy paperwork, airline policies, and grief — a burden that falls disproportionately on India's poorest states.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Owned Businesses in Britain Just Hit a Record. The Numbers Are Staggering.
nri-world.excerpt: A 60 per cent surge in a single year has pushed the count past 1,900 firms, £105 billion in turnover, and 200,000 jobs — making India the most consequential foreign investor Britain didn't see coming.
nri-world.image_caption: The Gherkin and surrounding skyscrapers in London's financial district
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin entrepreneurs and conglomerates are no longer peripheral players in Britain's economy — they are structural pillars, employing hundreds of thousands and paying hundreds of millions in tax, reshaping the NRI community's economic identity abroad.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Sent Its Largest-Ever Business Delegation to Canada. Here's What They Want.
nri-world.excerpt: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal led more than 100 companies to Toronto, with a $50 billion bilateral trade target on the table and the Indo-Canadian community positioned as the bridge.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal at an official event
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indo-Canadian community — 1.8 million strong — is central to both the diplomatic thaw and the commercial opportunity, with diaspora business leaders explicitly enlisted as accelerants for trade and investment flows.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Wealthy Indians Are Choosing Dubai Over Delhi. The Tax Maths Leaves Little Room for Debate.
nri-world.excerpt: Zero capital gains tax, rental yields three times higher than Mumbai's, and a dirham pegged to the dollar — the NRI investor class is voting with its chequebooks, and India's property market is noticing.
nri-world.image_caption: Skyscrapers of Dubai Marina reflected in the waterfront at dusk
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs are uniquely positioned to exploit the Dubai-India arbitrage — earning in dollars or dirhams, buying in a tax-free jurisdiction, and maintaining proximity to India for family and cultural ties. The shift reflects a maturing diaspora that evaluates real estate globally, not sentimentally.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Eight Indian Americans Just Won a Fellowship That Pays $90,000 for Being an Immigrant. Here's What They Study.
nri-world.excerpt: The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships picked 30 scholars from 1,800 applicants. More than a quarter are of Indian origin — a pattern that says something about the community's bet on education.
nri-world.image_caption: Graduates celebrating at a university commencement ceremony
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian Americans dominate a top immigrant fellowship, reflecting the diaspora's deep investment in education and research — even as the visa system they depend on faces political headwinds.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Top Aerospace Body Just Gave Its Highest Honour to India's Moon Mission. The Diaspora Noticed.
nri-world.excerpt: AIAA's Goddard Astronautics Award — previously reserved for the Hubble and James Webb telescope teams — went to ISRO's Chandrayaan-3. Ambassador Kwatra accepted it in Washington.
nri-world.image_caption: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander photographed on the lunar surface by the Pragyan rover
nri-world.nri_angle: The award validates the technical ecosystem that produced hundreds of thousands of Indian-origin aerospace professionals now working in America's own space enterprise.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian American Couple Pledged $1 Million to Feed America's Hungry. Their Movement Has Already Delivered 30 Million Meals.
nri-world.excerpt: The HungerMitao movement channels Indian diaspora resources into America's food banks. India's consul general attended the latest gala — a sign of how seriously New Delhi takes diaspora philanthropy.
nri-world.image_caption: Volunteers packing food donations at a community food bank
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian Americans are redirecting philanthropic energy from remittances to local American communities, building social capital and complicating the narrative that the diaspora only takes.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: AI Is Now America's Top Reason for Firing People. H-1B Workers Are Watching the Clock.
technology.excerpt: U.S. employers cut 97,000 jobs in May. AI was cited in 40 percent of them — the highest share ever recorded. For Indian tech workers on visas, the 60-day grace period has never felt shorter.
technology.image_caption: Empty desks at a technology company office following workforce reductions
technology.nri_angle: Indian H-1B visa holders make up the largest share of the tech workforce being cut. The 60-day grace period to find new sponsorship creates existential pressure when the entire sector is shedding jobs, and TCS just warned hiring will slow across Indian IT.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Cerebras Just IPO'd at $44 Billion. Nine Analysts Say Buy the Dip.
technology.excerpt: Wall Street initiated coverage on the dinner-plate-sized chip company with buy ratings across the board. The OpenAI deal, the inference bet, and the NVIDIA challenge are all priced in. Or are they?
technology.image_caption: A 12-inch silicon wafer — Cerebras builds its processors on entire wafers rather than cutting them into individual chips
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors with heavy exposure to AI and semiconductor stocks need to understand Cerebras as a potential disruptor to NVIDIA's dominance. The inference revolution it represents will also reshape the compute economics that Indian AI startups like Sarvam AI depend on.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI Just Filed for an IPO. A $4 Trillion Listing Wave Is About to Hit.
technology.excerpt: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI are heading to public markets within weeks of each other. The combined valuation rivals the GDP of Germany. History says mega-IPOs end badly for early buyers.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, whose company just filed a confidential S-1 for a public listing
technology.nri_angle: NRI portfolios are heavily concentrated in the same tech stocks that will compete for capital with these mega-IPOs. The $150-$200 billion in primary issuance could trigger a liquidity squeeze across NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Google — the backbone of most Indian American investment accounts.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS Chairman Says AI Agents Will Match Its 500,000 Headcount. Hiring Will Slow.
technology.excerpt: N. Chandrasekaran's AGM declaration crystallises what Indian IT has feared — the sector's labour-intensive model is being rewritten by AI, and entry-level hiring is the first casualty.
technology.image_caption: Corporate technology campus in Hyderabad, home to major Indian IT employers including TCS
technology.nri_angle: TCS and its peers sponsor thousands of H-1B visas annually. Slower hiring means fewer visa slots, and AI agents absorbing testing and maintenance work directly threatens the roles that brought hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers to America.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: US Senators Want to Plug the Last Hole in America's Chip Blockade. India Stands to Gain.
technology.excerpt: A bipartisan push to stop TSMC from making AI chips for Chinese shell companies accelerates the case for alternative fab capacity — and India's semiconductor mission is first in line.
technology.image_caption: TSMC semiconductor fabrication facility in Hsinchu, Taiwan
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian-American semiconductor engineers work at Intel, Qualcomm, and AMD. Tighter TSMC rules accelerate reshoring, creating more US-based chip jobs, while India's fab buildout is luring experienced NRI engineers back.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Just Ordered Three Million AI Chips From Intel. The Foundry Bet Is Paying Off.
technology.excerpt: Reports of a landmark manufacturing deal with Google — and a potential Nvidia contract — sent Intel shares up 12 per cent. Thousands of Indian engineers in Bangalore and Hyderabad are at the centre of the foundry pivot.
technology.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has led the company's foundry pivot since March 2025
technology.nri_angle: Intel's Bangalore and Hyderabad centres employ thousands of Indian engineers doing chip verification and physical design — the exact work that scales with foundry contracts. The pivot also creates new H-1B-eligible process engineering roles in Oregon and Arizona.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Zepto Just Filed for an $837 Million IPO. India's Grocery Wars Are Heading to the Stock Market.
technology.excerpt: The Stanford dropouts who bet on 10-minute delivery have doubled revenue to ₹22,624 crore. Losses doubled too. The July listing will test whether quick commerce has a profitable endgame.
technology.image_caption: Zepto, the Indian quick-commerce startup that filed for an 37 million IPO with SEBI (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors already holding Swiggy and Eternal shares now face a third listing in the same sector. Zepto's ad revenue growth hints at a platform play, but widening losses to ₹5,905 crore will test whether diaspora capital chases growth or demands profitability.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Intel Was Dying. Then AI Agents Needed CPUs. Lip-Bu Tan Is Riding the Accident.
technology.excerpt: The new CEO has fired a third of Intel's workforce, flattened its bureaucracy, and bet the company on a world where software agents need orchestration chips. Bengaluru's 10,000 Intel engineers are central to the plan.
technology.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has led the chipmaker's aggressive restructuring since taking the helm
technology.nri_angle: Intel employs over 10,000 engineers in Bengaluru, one of its largest global design centres. Indian Americans in semiconductor engineering built careers at Intel since the 1990s. Tan's 34% workforce cuts hit H-1B holders hard, but the survivors are working on Intel's most important product generation in decades.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: NVIDIA Dropped a Bomb on Qualcomm's PC Strategy. The Stock Says Everything.
technology.excerpt: Qualcomm's shares have cratered by double digits since RTX Spark's Computex debut. The company is retreating to $300 laptops. For 13,000 Indian engineers at Qualcomm, the pivot is personal.
technology.image_caption: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon, who faces a strategic reckoning as NVIDIA enters the PC chip market
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs approximately 13,000 people in India (Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai) and is a top H-1B employer in San Diego. A sustained stock decline erodes RSU values for Indian engineers who chose Qualcomm over FAANG. The growth story that justified premium compensation is now under serious strain.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Just Got Demoted. Taiwan and South Korea Stole Its Place in the Global AI Economy.
technology.excerpt: Foreign investors have pulled $26.4 billion from Indian equities in 2026 — more than all of 2025. The reason: India has no TSMC, and the AI boom is not waiting.
technology.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — India's equity market has fallen to seventh globally as AI-driven capital flows elsewhere
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors with dual India-US portfolios are watching the India allocation shrink while US tech surges. India's absence from the AI hardware supply chain — no TSMC, no SK Hynix — is driving a historic capital flight that directly affects diaspora wealth and the return-to-India investment thesis.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sriram Krishnan Is Leaving the White House. He Helped Write America's AI Playbook.
technology.excerpt: The Chennai-born technologist spent 18 months as the most influential Indian-American voice in US AI policy. His departure leaves a hole at the intersection of Silicon Valley and Washington.
technology.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, outgoing White House senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence
technology.nri_angle: Krishnan's White House role gave Indian-Americans unprecedented influence over AI policy affecting H-1B workers, chip exports, and the regulatory environment at companies where thousands of NRIs work. His exit raises questions about continued diaspora influence on US tech policy.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS Is Now Building the Offices That Steal Its Engineers. That's the Point.
technology.excerpt: India's largest IT company launches a dedicated business unit to help multinationals build AI-native Global Capability Centres — the same centres that have been draining its talent pool for years.
technology.image_caption: TCS SIPCOT IT Park in Chennai, headquarters of India's largest IT services company
technology.nri_angle: GCCs are reshaping Indian tech careers — paying 15-40% more than traditional IT services, hiring 4x faster, and offering multinational work without leaving India. For NRIs evaluating return-to-India options, TCS's pivot signals that the future of Indian tech employment is inside GCCs, not servicing them.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Most Powerful Obesity Drug Ever Tested Just Crushed Sleep Apnea and Knee Pain in a Single Trial. South Asians Are in the Crosshairs.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide, which targets three hormones at once, reduced sleep apnea severity by 61 per cent and knee pain by 73 per cent while delivering 28 per cent body weight loss. For a community with the highest rates of metabolic disease in the world, this is not just another headline.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Eli Lilly headquarters in Indianapolis, Indiana — home of the company behind retatrutide
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It Is Not How Much You Walk. It Is How You Walk. A New Study Says the Difference Is 67 Per Cent.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A UK Biobank study of over 6,000 adults found that consolidating the same number of steps into continuous 10-to-15-minute walks — instead of scattering them across the day — reduced cardiovascular events by up to 67 per cent. For South Asians, who carry the world's highest heart disease burden, this reframes everything.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Morning walkers in a park — new research shows continuous walking sessions protect the heart far more than scattered steps throughout the day
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: American Doctors Are Finally Getting Nutrition Training. It Still Will Not Cover Your Dadi's Kitchen.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Seventy-three US medical schools have pledged 40 hours of nutrition education. For South Asian patients, that is still not the right 40 hours.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A traditional Indian thali — US medical nutrition training still doesn't account for South Asian dietary traditions (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Vaccine That Prevents Cancer Before It Starts Just Got the Green Light. Here Is Why South Asians Should Care.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Oxford and Moderna's INTERCEPT-Lynch trial is the first mRNA vaccine designed to stop hereditary cancers from ever forming. The first patient will be dosed this summer.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A vaccine being administered — mRNA technology is now being tested to prevent cancer before it starts (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A South Asian Man Reversed His Diabetes for a Decade. He Did It Without Giving Up Indian Food.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Frontiers in Nutrition case study documents ten years of medication-free type 2 diabetes remission using a culturally adapted low-carbohydrate vegetarian diet — and it may hold the key to the diaspora's biggest health crisis.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A blood glucose monitoring test — the daily reality for millions of South Asians living with type 2 diabetes
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Antibiotic Resistance Genes Now Contaminate Every Ocean on Earth. India's Coastline Is One of the Most Exposed.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A three-year Italian-led study found drug-resistant DNA, microplastics, and forever chemicals across all major ocean basins — with the highest concentrations near populated coasts and shipping routes.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Antimicrobial resistance has spread to every major ocean basin, including waters far from coastlines (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Found the Molecular Switch That Drives Alzheimer's Brain Inflammation. It Can Be Turned Off.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Scripps Research team identified a single chemical modification on the STING protein that locks the brain's immune system into overdrive. Blocking it preserved memory-critical synapses in mice.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A PET scan comparing a healthy brain (left) with one affected by Alzheimer's disease — researchers have now identified the molecular switch driving the inflammation (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Gut Bacterium Can Decide Whether You Survive Sepsis. Your Diet May Have Already Chosen Sides.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Nature study found that one bacterial strain in the gut dropped survival rates from near-certain to 10 per cent. The implications for South Asian hospital patients and diaspora diets are profound.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Rod-shaped bacteria viewed under high magnification microscopy
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Crease in Your Earlobe May Be Warning You About Your Heart. South Asians Should Pay Attention.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A diagonal line across the earlobe — known as Frank's sign — has been linked to coronary artery disease for over 50 years. A 2026 diagnostic model says it may be one of the strongest independent predictors of cardiac risk, and the community most vulnerable to heart disease is the least likely to know about it.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Coronary artery disease — a condition that research increasingly links to visible markers such as the diagonal earlobe crease known as Frank's sign

lifestyle-health.title: Global Mental Health Just Hit Its Lowest Recorded Level. The Diaspora's Silence Makes It Worse.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The 2026 AXA Mind Health Report surveyed 19,000 adults across 18 countries and found 46 per cent are languishing or struggling. Among younger generations, that number is 59 per cent. South Asian Americans remain among the least likely to seek help — and the most likely to turn to AI chatbots instead.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The World Health Organization headquarters — the AXA-Ipsos Mind Health Report shows global mental health at its lowest recorded level

lifestyle-health.title: Laughter Rewires Your Child's Brain Faster Than Flashcards. The Science Says It Is Not Even Close.
